message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-2/((1+sqrt(1+r))*(2+r))","derivation":"Retain the source-only B(r)=-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) which cancels the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r to machine epsilon when u=0. Add C(r)=-2/((1+sqrt(1+r))*(2+r)) to cancel the linear-in-u cross coupling in the full residual E=(2g+g^2-r)+2*u*g. Derivation: writing g=r/2+r^2*B+u*r*C (inner region, chi=1), the u^1 coefficient of E is r*(1+2rB+C(2+r)). Setting this to zero gives C=-(1+2rB)/(2+r). With B=-1/(2(1+sqrt(1+r))^2), we get 1+2rB=2/(1+sqrt(1+r)), hence C=-2/((1+sqrt(1+r))(2+r)). Both B and C are C-infinity on r>-1, an open neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle |r|<=1/2. The remaining u^2 term is O(r*u^2), reducing the dominant residual from O(r*u)~1.5e-6 to O(r*u^2)~1e-8 for the observed UNIFORM rows (r~1.9e-4, u~7.8e-3). The u=0 cancellation is unchanged; the formula adds no new singularities.","inspect":[{"file_id":"CALC/initial.json","limit":4096,"offset":0}],"note":"Successor should verify: (1) at stage p2 with tau^3 targets, confirm the cross residual drops from ~1e-6 to ~1e-8 or better on UNIFORM rows; (2) the LEFT/RIGHT/BOTH edge rows with |r|>1/2 (e.g., r=-1.0 at x=1/8) remain outside chi_r support and receive only the linear r/2 step unchanged; (3) rows with |u|>1/4 (e.g., z=-3 giving u=-4) are outside chi_u support and get no nonlinear correction; (4) the C term introduces no new domain singularity since (1+sqrt(1+r))(2+r)>0 for all r>-1; (5) the u^2 remainder r*C*(rC+2)*u^2 is not cancelled and will appear as the leading residual at successor stages; (6) do not interpret finite-grid zero residuals as a uniform analytic bound over the full rectangle or as a PDE estimate."}
